bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-639 IDOR in the Calendar Event Frontend Dialog. GET /ccm/calendar/view_event/{bID}/{occurrence_id} is handled by Concrete\Controller\Dialog\Frontend\Event, which extends Backend\UserInterface so shouldRunControllerTask()/getViewObject() call canAccess(); that method always returns true. view() only requires Block::getByID($bID) to be a calendar block, then loads EventOccurrence::getByID($occurrence_id) with no check that the occurrence belongs to the block's calendar and no canViewCalendar() on either the block calendar or the occurrence's calendar. A public calendar block is therefore a pivot: an attacker substitutes a private calendar's occurrence id and the dialog view renders title, description, date, page link, and event attributes via the public block's lightbox property list (getPropertyValue). Fixed in 9.5.1 by requiring canViewCalendar() on the block-bound calendar before loading the occurrence.
flaw_origin: On 2017-11-01 Andrew Embler first wrote concrete/controllers/dialog/frontend/event.php while migrating the core-team Calendar add-on into the CMS (commit 66f16af85c73dc35d55302634ecd4f6572123fd3). That first public write already implemented the dialog as a Backend UserInterface controller whose canAccess() is `return true` and whose view($bID, $occurrence_id) loads any EventOccurrence by user-controlled id after only a calendar-block-type check. The 2017-11-06 namespace correction (97ca3e10) and later router extraction did not change those lines. No finer public git member of the pre-core marketplace add-on is reconstructable; the immediate parent tree lacks the file.

reasoning: CVE-2026-8204/GHSA-x2fp-hj8c-mmxh is a published Concrete CMS CNA record, not withdrawn. The mechanism is the frontend event dialog: canAccess always true, user-controlled bID plus occurrence_id, EventOccurrence loaded without calendar authorization or occurrence-to-block binding, so a public calendar block discloses private event fields through the lightbox renderer. git log -L/-S/--follow/--diff-filter=A all identify 66f16af85c73dc35d55302634ecd4f6572123fd3 as the first public write of those lines; its parent 97b1daf25ba487a2b9ec53897f47dd4026eec8cd is a real commit whose tree lacks the file. The 2017 bulk calendar migration is an add of new paths rather than a reconstructable squash of public members; GitHub org/code search does not expose an earlier public add-on history for this controller, so this first-write is the smallest surviving public BIC. Later namespace/router/mode commits do not rewrite the flawed canAccess or getByID logic. The BIC precedes 8.3.0 and 9.5.0; the 9.5.1 landing f22b9dff59454391a50a255a39995bf635deea9e (decomposed member 6f7d4964a4ad627071697721c0ed8c77af1644c7, H1 3641132) adds canViewCalendar on the block calendar.
